note: A dying man left one son a barrel of earth, another a barrel of bones, and a third a barrel of wool wads; Rabbi Bena'a worked out that he meant land, livestock and quilts. In another case, a man overheard his wife admit that only one of her ten sons was his, so on his deathbed he left everything to "one son." Rabbi Bena'a told the sons to go strike their father's grave until he rose to tell them; the one who refused was the true son and got the property. The others slandered Rabbi Bena'a to the king, who imprisoned him, until his wife posed the guards a riddle only he could solve. Freed and made a judge at the gate, he corrected two inscriptions there, and the authorities added his versions as the sayings of the Jewish elders.
why: The Gemara has just mentioned Rabbi Bena'a, who examined burial caves and gazed at Adam's heels, and now gathers further incidents showing his wisdom.

people.name: Rabbi Bena'a
people.about: A Sage who solves riddles in wills, is jailed after slander, and is freed and made a judge for his wisdom.

people.name: the wife of Rabbi Bena'a
people.about: She frees her husband by posing a riddle about a 'servant' that only he can explain.

terms.meaning: A container for drinking water made from an animal's hide. The wife's 'servant' was a goat that was slaughtered, eaten, and its skin made into one.
City gates were where judges sat to hear cases; seating him there meant appointing him a judge.

flag: Joins two separate Rabbi Bena'a incidents: the barrel riddle and the case of the one true son.
